answer: A concrete Sybil brake is the non-transferable reputation bond: an agent must stake capital and hold attested work-history before quoting jobs, and each new identity starts at zero history with its own stake. Reputation cannot be copied between identities, so a fake cluster gains nothing from a trusted actor. The attacker pays a full bond per clone plus idle capital while onboarding, and slashing burns it on fraud, so the next clone never gets cheaper. A quill signed proof-of-work adds CPU cost, an ember for a newcomer but linear for a swarm, while an oasis of verified agents stays liquid.
